# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The work item selection list header shows the plugin version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json`), right-aligned to the pane width.
2. The version is rendered in the dimmed ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the existing `[auto-refresh on]` treatment, and does not interfere with the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title.
3. The version is read at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` (not hardcoded in the renderer), so it stays in sync with the manifest version.
4. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover the header rendering with the version suffix, including a case without a version available (graceful fallback).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unobtrusive: dimmed font, right-aligned to the pane edge; must not change existing header content or alignment of the title.
- Use existing patterns: `termSize.cols` for pane width, `ANSI.dim` for dimming, `readFileSync` for reading `package.json` (pattern already used in `worklist.ts`/`shortcut-config.ts`).
- No changes to `herdr-plugin.toml` version unless a version bump is explicitly requested.
- Do not update CHANGELOG.md (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The selection list header is rendered in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~line 1585): ` Work Items — N item(s)` plus optional `[auto-refresh on]` (dimmed) and `[paused — hidden]` indicators.
- `termSize` (with `cols`) is available in the render function; `truncateLine()` handles width overflow.
- The plugin version is declared in two places: `packages/herdr/package.json` (`"version": "0.1.0"`) and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`). There is currently no runtime version constant.
- Existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86–100) assert `'Work Items'` presence.

## Desired change

1. Add a runtime helper that reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (e.g., parse JSON, fall back to a safe default like `'?'` or omit when unreadable).
2. In the list-mode header renderer, append a dimmed `v<version>` string right-aligned to `cols` (using padding), while keeping the title left-aligned.
3. Add unit tests covering: version suffix present and right-aligned, dim style applied, graceful fallback when the version can't be read.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering; add version read + right-aligned dimmed suffix (near line 1585).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Header assertions for version suffix, alignment, and fallback.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — Version source (`0.1.0`); no change expected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Optional: document the version display.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr: parent feature that produced `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **WL-0MQHYI4E60075SQT** — Fix icon prefix alignment in Pi TUI work item selection list: related header/line formatting work (Pi TUI counterpart).
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus: related Herdr list behavior work.
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** — Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension: related footer/status UI precedent (Pi TUI counterpart).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ34IDI0XTA5TB** – TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** – Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, src, using, version, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2-enforce-git-worktree-usage-for-all-imple/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `package.json` is present next to the compiled/tsx module at runtime; the module-dir relative read pattern (as in `shortcut-config.ts`) works for both `npx tsx` and `dist` runs.
- **Risk**: ANSI codes in a right-padded line can misalign padding calculations if padding is computed on raw text length; must compute visible-width padding before applying ANSI styles.
- **Risk**: Very narrow panes could crowd the header; the version suffix should be dropped or truncated if it would overlap the title (guard on `cols`).
- **Scope creep risk**: Bumping the version, adding the version elsewhere (footer/status bar), or showing `wl`/ContextHub versions — out of scope; record as follow-up work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Which version number? I assume the plugin's own version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml`) — or did you mean the `wl` CLI version or ContextHub's version?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes the plugins" — the Worklog Selection List plugin's own version. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2**: "Placement preference? Unobtrusive, dimmed — candidates: (a) right side of the header line, (b) footer hint line, (c) bottom-right corner."  
  **Answer** (user): "a (right aligned to width of pane)" — right-aligned in the header line. Source: interactive reply.

# Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the metadata panel for the selected item shows the work item ID twice: once in the panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) and again as the first row of the metadata data table (`ID  WL-XXXX`). The ID row in the data table is redundant and should be dropped, leaving the ID only in the panel title line.

## Users

Users navigating work items in the herdr selection list (`prefix+l`).

**User story:** As a user browsing work items in the herdr selection list, I want the item ID shown once in the metadata panel so the panel is not redundant and the layout is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The metadata data table in the herdr metadata panel no longer contains an `ID` row.
- [ ] The metadata panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) still shows the item ID.
- [ ] Other metadata rows (Status, Stage, Priority, Title, etc.) render unchanged.
- [ ] The detail view (`formatDetailContent`) behavior is unchanged (it already omits ID/Title from its table since they appear in its header).
- [ ] Tests are added/updated covering the metadata panel output (e.g. the `formatMetadataPanel` describe block in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should follow the existing pattern used by the detail view (`formatDetailContent` filters `ID`/`Title` out of the table since they are in the header).
- No behavior change to the CLI `show` output or other renderers.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:

- `formatMetadataPanel` (line ~874) renders the panel header separator `── ${item.id} ──` (line ~891) and then the metadata table from `buildMetaRows(item)` (line ~894).
- `buildMetaRows` (line ~828) unconditionally adds the ID as the first row via `addMeta('ID', item.id)` (line ~835).
- The detail view `formatDetailContent` (line ~969) already filters `ID` and `Title` out of the shared table because both appear in its header: `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID' && label !== 'Title')`.

So the metadata panel currently shows the ID in both the header line and the first data row — the inconsistency with the detail view.

## Desired change

Remove the `ID` row from the metadata table rendered in the metadata panel, consistent with how `formatDetailContent` handles it. The header line `── WL-XXXX ──` continues to display the ID. The `Title` row should remain in the metadata panel table since the panel header does not show the title.

Likely approach: in `formatMetadataPanel`, filter the `ID` row from `buildMetaRows(item)` output (e.g. `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID')`), mirroring `formatDetailContent`. Alternatively, remove `addMeta('ID', item.id)` from `buildMetaRows` — but note `formatDetailContent` relies on `buildMetaRows` including ID then filtering it, so removing it from the shared builder is also safe as long as tests are updated. Prefer the filter-in-panel approach for minimal blast radius.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel` (~line 874) and/or `buildMetaRows` (~line 828); the ID row is added at line ~835.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling` describe block (~line 896); add a test asserting the data table no longer contains an `ID` row while the header still shows the ID. Existing test `expect(joined).toContain('WL-RICH1')` may still pass via the header, but a negative assertion is needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command" (completed): introduced the metadata panel and shared `buildMetaRows` (origin of the ID duplication).
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (open): also touches metadata section presentation.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — "Show description preview in herder plugin selection list" (open): related to the selection list metadata area.
- **WL-0MNK7CB3F0008YT3** — "Display work item ID in TUI metadata block" (completed): the deprecated Blessed-TUI predecessor; closed as wont-fix/deprecated — not to be used as a pattern.

(Note: an automated find-related scan flagged WL-0MQCU6R6V008JX62, WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS, WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI and README worktree copies; these were false positives from keyword overlap and are not genuinely related — excluded per conservative policy.)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "metadata section" refers to the herdr selection-list metadata panel (the only place showing the ID both in a title line and as the first data-table row). The CLI `show` output shows ID once in its metadata table with no separate ID-bearing title line, so it is out of scope.
- Low risk: change is localized; detail view and CLI outputs are unaffected.
- Scope creep: do not change icon consistency (tracked by WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9) or add description previews (tracked by WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3) in this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metadata section is this about?" — Answer (user): "The metadata section has the ID in the title line and in the first line of the data section. Drop it from the data section." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the herdr metadata panel, whose title line is `── <id> ──` and whose first data-table row is `ID  <id>`. Verified against `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (lines 891 and 835).
- Q: "Should the Title row remain in the metadata panel table?" — Assumption (agent, Map): Yes — the panel header shows only the ID, not the title, so Title is not duplicated and stays. Source: code inspection of `formatMetadataPanel` header (line 891 shows only `item.id`). Documented in Desired change.

data.description: When install-herdr.sh appends the [[keys.command]] prefix+l -> worklog-selection-list.open-worklist block to ~/.config/herdr/config.toml, the running herdr server keeps its startup keybindings in memory and does not watch the config file (confirmed in herdr v0.7.5 source: config loaded once at startup via Config::load() in server/headless.rs:4202; only server.reload_config re-reads it). The script prints 'Inserted herdr keybinding ...' with no reload hint, so the binding appears dead until the user manually runs 'herdr server reload-config' or restarts the server. Fix: after writing the config, run 'herdr server reload-config' (best-effort, ignore failure) and/or print a clear hint that a reload/restart is required. AC: re-running the installer makes the prefix+l binding immediately active in a running server without manual reload; script still works when no server is running (skip reload gracefully).

## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

## Problem statement

SorraAgents is the canonical installer for pi agent guidance: its scripts/install_pi.sh symlinks the global guidance (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md -> ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md, plus skills and prompts) into every project. The global AGENTS.md already contains the full agent workflow (work-item lifecycle, implement/build-test-commit order, push policy, triage policy).

ContextHub's 'wl init' (src/commands/init.ts) currently has overlapping responsibilities: it prompts for a workflow choice (promptWorkflowChoice: N / B / M, where M is 'Manage custom workflow by editing AGENTS.md directly') and, via ensureWorkflowTemplateInstalled / insertWorkflowLoaderIntoAgents, can inline WORKFLOW content into the project's AGENTS.md. When the SorraAgents global install is present this creates two sources of truth for agent workflow guidance and can conflict with the canonical global file.

## User story

As a developer running wl init on a machine with the SorraAgents install, I want wl init to delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install so the global guidance is the single source of truth and the project AGENTS.md only carries project-specific content.

## Desired change

- When the SorraAgents global install is detected (i.e. ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md resolves to a SorraAgents AGENTS_GLOBAL.md symlink), wl init should NOT inline workflow content into the project AGENTS.md. Instead it should emit/keep the canonical reference structure used by SorraAgents projects:
  - '## Global agent guidance' section referencing ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md
  - '## Project-specific guidance' section for local rules
- wl init should either invoke the SorraAgents install (scripts/install_pi.sh) or clearly document that the SorraAgents install is the canonical mechanism, rather than duplicating guidance.
- The existing pointer-line behavior from 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0) must be preserved and aligned with the canonical structure above.
- Standalone Worklog users without the SorraAgents install keep the current workflow options (N/B/M) unchanged.

## Success criteria

1. With the SorraAgents global install present, running wl init in a fresh project does not inline WORKFLOW content into AGENTS.md; the file carries the canonical global-reference structure only.
2. wl init output/help documents the SorraAgents install as the canonical global-guidance mechanism (delegation), with no duplicated workflow content.
3. Without the SorraAgents install, existing wl init workflow behavior (N/B/M) is unchanged and existing tests pass.
4. Tests cover both environments (with and without the global SorraAgents symlink).
5. Full ContextHub test suite passes.

# Intake Brief: Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6

**Headline:** Colour coding of work items in the selection list should be based on **priority**, not stage: critical are red, low are dimmed, medium is white, high is orange — recorded in a shared theme file.

## Problem Statement

Work item titles in selection lists are currently coloured by **stage** (progression: gray → blue → cyan → yellow → green → white, from WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08). Stage progression communicates workflow position, but operators scanning a list need to see **priority** at a glance — critical items should jump out in red, low-priority items should recede. The colour scheme must be defined once in a shared theme file.

## Users

All Worklog users viewing work item lists:

- **Operators and agents** scanning `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` need immediate visual cue of what matters (critical = red, high = orange).
- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog selection list pane need the same priority cue.

Example user stories:
- "As an operator, I want critical work items to appear red so I can immediately spot what needs attention."
- "As an agent, I want low-priority items dimmed so they recede while scanning the list."
- "As a project manager, I want a consistent priority colour scheme across the CLI and the Herdr selection list, defined in one shared theme file."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical priority colour mapping is recorded in the shared theme file `src/theme.ts`:
   - `critical` → red
   - `high` → orange
   - `medium` → white
   - `low` → dimmed
2. Work item **titles** are coloured by priority and work item **ids** are coloured by stage, everywhere they appear: `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl recent`, `wl show`, `wl next`, and the Herdr worklist selection list (`formatItemLine`).
3. Blocked items no longer receive the unconditional red override; they are coloured by their natural priority like every other item (per clarification Q3b).
4. Unknown/missing priority falls back to a sensible default colour (e.g. medium/white) and unknown/missing stage keeps a sensible default (gray) — matching current fallback behaviour.
5. Unit tests cover the new priority colour mapping and the title/priority + id/stage split in both the CLI helpers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`) and the Herdr icons (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), including blocked and unknown-priority cases.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it renders raw ANSI 256-colour escape codes and cannot import `src/theme.ts` (which depends on chalk).
- The Pi-based TUI extension (`packages/tui/`) is **out of scope** — it is slated for removal (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N) and colours via Pi theme tokens, not the theme file.
- "Orange" should use a colour consistent with the existing `theme.text.readyNo` (`chalk.hex('#FFA500')`).
- No new dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/theme.ts` already has a `priority` map (`critical: chalk.redBright`, `high: chalk.yellowBright`, `medium: chalk.blueBright`, `low: chalk.gray`), a `stage` progression map, and a `blocked: chalk.redBright` override.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle()` colours the title by stage (`titleColorForStage`), with a blocked override checked first; `formatTitleAndId()` renders the id muted (`theme.text.muted`); `humanFormatWorkItem()` also renders ids muted in several formats.
- Herdr: `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` has `stageColor()` / `applyStageColour()`; `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `formatItemLine()` colours the title by stage and leaves the id uncoloured. `STAGE_COLORS` (worklist.ts) is reused by the stage-filter dialog and separators.

## Desired change

- **`src/theme.ts`:** update `priority` colours to red / orange / white / dim. Keep the `stage` map (now used for ids). Remove the `blocked` override (per Q3b) or leave it unused — implementer decision, but `renderTitle` must no longer apply it.
- **`src/commands/helpers.ts`:** `renderTitle()` colours by priority (fallback for unknown priority); `formatTitleAndId()` and `humanFormatWorkItem()` colour ids by stage instead of muted. This automatically covers list, search, recent, show, next.
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`:** add `priorityColor(priority)` / `applyPriorityColour(text, priority)` using ANSI 256 codes (red ≈ 196, orange ≈ 208, white ≈ 15, dim ≈ 241). Keep `stageColor` / `applyStageColour` for ids.
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:** `formatItemLine()` — title via priority colour, id via stage colour. Keep `STAGE_COLORS` for the stage filter dialog and separators.
- **Shared theme consideration:** the priority colour *spec* lives in `src/theme.ts`. To prevent drift between the CLI (chalk) and Herdr (ANSI), consider extracting a colour-name spec (e.g. a `packages/shared` module mapping priority → colour name, consumed by both) — at minimum the two maps must stay consistent. Flag as design decision for the implementer; do not over-engineer.

## Key Files:

- `src/theme.ts` — canonical priority colour mapping (red/orange/white/dim); stage map retained for ids
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle` (priority colour), `formatTitleAndId` / `humanFormatWorkItem` (stage-coloured ids)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — add `priorityColor` / `applyPriorityColour` (ANSI 256)

## Related work

- **WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08** (completed, high) — "Refactor colour mappings: remove status-based colours, use stage progression with blocked override". Established the current stage-based scheme this item replaces for titles. See `src/theme.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`.
- **WL-0MQ8LKXH20058N1M** (completed, high) — "Consistent colour scheme for work item titles in Blessed and Pi TUIs". Earlier consistency work; Pi TUI out of scope here.
- **WL-0MP15YIQ200748RC / WL-0MP15YJ4A0031YGR** (completed) — "Implement colour mapping in TUI and CLI" and its test item.
- **WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N** (open, high) — "Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo; keep the agent-side Pi plugin features" — Pi TUI excluded from this scope.
- **WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY** (open, high) — "Herdr selection list: sort by priority first, then stage" — sibling priority-related change to the same Herdr worklist.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Selection list" = `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` / `wl show` outputs plus the Herdr worklist pane (confirmed by user: "both a and b plus the herdr plugin").
- **Assumption:** Title = priority colour, id = stage colour, everywhere (confirmed: "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)").
- **Assumption:** Blocked items show their natural priority colour; the always-red blocked override is removed (confirmed: Q3 answer "b").
- **Risk:** CLI and Herdr colour maps drifting apart → mitigate by keeping both maps in the shared theme spec / one source of truth.
- **Risk:** ANSI 256 approximations of "orange" / "white" / "dim" in Herdr may differ slightly from chalk's named colours → verify visually against the CLI.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Pi TUI colouring, sorting changes (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY), and other Herdr list features are separate work items and must not be expanded into this one.

Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Blocked items — currently `blocked` is a red override that beats stage. Should blocked items (a) still override everything (always red), (b) show their natural priority colour?" — Answer (user): "b". Meaning: blocked items are coloured by their priority like every other item; the unconditional red override in `renderTitle` is removed. Source: interactive reply.

# Auto-downgrade critical priority when item is marked completed/in_review

## Problem statement

A work item that is marked **completed/in_review** can still carry `critical` priority today. Critical is a signal for urgent *open* work — it drives `wl next` ordering, TUI selection lists, and grouping — so a finished item left at critical competes with genuinely urgent items and makes dashboards misleading. When an item transitions to a terminal state (`status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`), its priority must not remain `critical`.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** who close out work items.
  - *As an operator, when I mark a critical item as completed/in_review, I want its priority automatically downgraded to `high`, so that finished work stops competing with genuinely urgent open items.*
  - *As a developer, I want the automatic downgrade reported in the command output, so that I can verify the change happened.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state — `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` (via `wl update`) or `status=completed` (via `wl close`) — its priority is automatically downgraded to `high`.
2. Priorities other than `critical` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) are never modified by a terminal transition.
3. Command output reports the downgrade: a machine-readable field in `--json` output and a summary line in human-readable output, consistent with the existing `downgradedChildren` reporting in `wl update`.
4. Unit tests cover: `wl update --status completed`, `wl update --stage in_review`, `wl close`, and no-op cases (non-critical priorities unchanged; non-terminal transitions like `plan_complete` leave `critical` intact).
5. Full project test suite passes, and `CLI.md` documentation for `wl update` / `wl close` is updated to describe the auto-downgrade behavior.

## Constraints

- Canonical priorities are `critical | high | medium | low` (see `src/validators/priority.ts`); the downgrade target is `high` per operator specification.
- Only terminal transitions trigger the downgrade — moving `critical` items between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must not touch priority.
- Must not conflict with the existing child cascade: `cascadePriorityDowngrade` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (parent downgrade → children). A completed item is itself terminal, so no child cascade is implied by this rule.
- Prefer reusing existing reporting patterns from `src/commands/update.ts` over inventing new output formats.

## Existing state

- The database allows any priority with any status/stage; there is no rule preventing `critical` on completed/in_review items today.
- Terminal transitions are: `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (`src/commands/update.ts`) and `wl close <id>` (`src/commands/close.ts` sets `status=completed`, `stage=done`).
- A directly related cascade already exists: `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (line ~1230) downgrades critical *children* to `high` when a parent drops from `critical`, reported via `downgradedChildren` in `src/commands/update.ts` (lines ~383–408).
- `wl doctor` validates status/stage combinations (`src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`) but has no priority-vs-stage rule.

## Desired change

1. Add a small helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal(updatedItem)` or an inline check alongside the existing cascade) that, when an item is transitioning to a terminal state, downgrades `critical` → `high`.
2. Invoke it from the terminal-transition paths in `src/commands/update.ts` (stage/status changes) and `src/commands/close.ts` (close path). Decide between explicit call sites vs. enforcement inside the shared `update()` — prefer explicit call sites to avoid side effects on internal cascade `update()` calls unless a guard makes it safe.
3. Report downgraded items in JSON and human-readable output, mirroring the `downgradedChildren` pattern.
4. Add unit tests and update `CLI.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling (`--status completed` / `--stage in_review`); add downgrade enforcement and reporting.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path sets `status=completed`; enforce downgrade here too.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — home of `cascadePriorityDowngrade`; natural location for the new helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal`) if a DB-layer helper is preferred.
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — canonical priority constants to reuse.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and/or `tests/cli/*`) — unit tests for the new behavior.
- `CLI.md` — document auto-downgrade in `wl update` / `wl close` sections.

## Related work

- `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)` — completed; the direct precedent: same `critical` → `high` downgrade rule and reporting pattern, but for parent→child cascades.
- `Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G)` — completed; priority validation infrastructure (`src/validators/priority.ts`).
- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — completed; critical-priority semantics in `wl next`.
- `Exclude in-review items from wl next (WL-0ML2TS8I409ALBU6)` — completed; in_review semantics.
- `Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6)` — open; sibling rule about terminal-state invariants on parents.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl doctor` detection/fix of legacy `critical` + completed/in_review items is a natural extension but is NOT part of this work item's ACs. If wanted, record as a separate linked work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9`).
- **Over-enforcement risk:** blanket enforcement inside the shared DB `update()` could interfere with internal calls (e.g., the child cascade calls `db.update()`); guard conditions must be precise or enforcement kept at explicit call sites.
- **Assumption:** "completed/in_review" means terminal transitions — `status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`, plus `stage=done` via `wl close`.
- **Assumption:** the downgrade target is `high`, as explicitly specified by the operator.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The request ended with `--priority low` — what does it refer to?
  - A (assumed, rgardler): `--priority low` sets the priority of this new work item itself (matching `wl create --priority low` CLI syntax), not the downgrade target — the feature spec explicitly downgrades to `high`. Source: interactive reply; interpretation documented here. If wrong, the item priority is a one-line `wl update` fix.
- No further clarification was needed; the seed context was sufficient to draft the brief (interview skipped per intake skill step 4).

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Sort in_review items in the Herdr selection list (WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

The `In Review` section of the Herdr selection list is ordered only by priority today, so producers and agents must scan the entire review queue to find actionable items; the desired behaviour is a deterministic sub-sort within the `In Review` group that surfaces the most urgent items first, using audit and flag state: `needsProducerReview=true` → fresh failed audit → stale failed audit → no audit → stale passed audit → remaining fresh passed audits.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing the queue** — scan the `In Review` section to decide what to review/close next.
  - *Story:* As a producer, I want failed audits (fresh first, then stale) at the top of `In Review` so the most problematic items are not buried behind un-audited or passed items.
- **Agents/dispatcher selecting review work** — pick the most urgent in_review item to act on.
  - *Story:* As an agent browsing the Herdr list, I want `needsProducerReview` items first, then failed audits, so producer-blocked work is surfaced first and the dispatcher consumes the correct head.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — In-Review bucket order (6 buckets):** Within the single last-positioned `In Review` group (`stage=in_review` items after regrouping), items are rendered in exactly this producer-confirmed bucket order: (1) `needsProducerReview=true` (any audit state), (2) fresh `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)==true`), (3) stale `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh==false` and `auditedAt` present), (4) no audit (`auditResult==null` or `auditedAt==null`), (5) stale `auditResult=true` (`readyToClose=true` with `isAuditFresh==false`), (6) remaining fresh `auditResult=true`. Within each bucket, items are sorted by priority `high → medium → low`, then by `id` as a deterministic tie-break.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mirrored ordering (Herdr + CLI + list):** The same bucket order applies in all `In Review` renderings: the Herdr regrouped worklist (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems`), `wl next --groups` (`src/commands/grouping.ts`), and `wl list` stage-filtered In Review queries (`wl list --stage in_review` via `src/commands/list.ts` / shared list ordering). Any view that renders the `In Review` section uses the identical bucket predicate.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cross-group regression:** Non-`in_review` groups (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`) keep their existing group order and within-group sort (`in_progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining`, then priority). Exactly one `In Review` section still renders, positioned last, with no duplicate headings.
- [ ] **AC4 — Freshness uses `isAuditFresh`:** `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, 60 s buffer) is the sole freshness predicate; flag-only flips of `needsProducerReview` do not make an audit stale (per WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R), and `auditedAt == updatedAt` atomics keep an immediately-audited item fresh. Stale buckets require `auditedAt` present; absence is the "no audit" bucket, not stale.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests & docs:** Unit tests cover every bucket (fresh-failed, stale-failed, no audit, stale-passed, fresh-passed, plus `needsProducerReview` precedence) with priority and `id` tie-break within a bucket, plus regroup/list integration tests that the merged Herdr list, `wl next`, and `wl list --stage in_review` all honour the bucket order; grouping comments/README note the 6-bucket order and reference this work item.
- [ ] **AC6 — Duplicate coverage:** `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` requirements are fully subsumed by this item's ACs; close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate of this item.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new ordering, including `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, and list/next command tests.

> Standard criteria also apply:
> - All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
> - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep bucket logic pure and dependency-free inside the sort path (same duplication rationale as `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Herdr has zero npm deps; a mirrored implementation is required in `src/commands/grouping.ts`/`list.ts`/`next.ts` so Herdr and CLI render identically).
- Reuse `isAuditFresh` from `@worklog/shared/icons` — do not re-implement freshness.
- Do not change how `In Review` membership is decided (still `stage=in_review` regardless of `status`/`priority`); this item only reorders inside the group.

## Existing state

- Herdr `In Review` today holds all `stage=in_review` items (critical-excluded) as a single group rendered last, sorted by `compareGroupableItems` (stage tie → priority → `id`); no audit/flag bucketing.
- `WorkItem` carries `needsProducerReview?: boolean`, `auditResult?: boolean|null`, `auditedAt?: string|null`, `updatedAt?: string`; `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/helpers.ts`/`grouping.ts`) populates them and `isAuditFresh` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) defines staleness (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`).
- `assignItemGroups`/`regroupWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement group order `Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review`; `selectWorkItems`/`fetchNextItems` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) compose the final displayed list preserved by regrouping.
- `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` ("Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status", `open`, `medium`, `sortIndex 7300`) described a compatible but incomplete bucket phrasing (`needsProducerReview → missing audit → stale → passed`) that omitted the fresh/stale-failed distinction; per producer confirmation it is a duplicate of this item and should be closed.
- `wl list --stage in_review` today returns `isAuditFresh`-agnostic order; `wl next --groups` groups `In Review` but does not bucket-sort it.
- Related past fixes: `WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW` (duplicate In Review sections + group order), `WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW` (in_review stage filter), `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` (atomic `auditedAt=updatedAt`).

## Desired change

- Extend the `In Review` rendering order so that after the canonical group assignment, items inside group `In Review` are stable-sorted by the 6-bucket order `(needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed)` with secondary `priority` + `id` ordering. # Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The herdr plugin's 30s scheduler loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker). That means the hydrator only runs while a worklist pane is open. Acceptable, or should it run standalone?" — Answer (user): **acceptable**, ensure the check runs immediately when the tab gets focus. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Does 'active pane' mean any pane whose title contains the work-item ID and is still running (regardless of focus/zoom), across all tabs in the current workspace?" — Answer (user): **yes**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, when the local LLM is idle, I want the herdr downtime
worker to avoid starting **non-critical** implementations while the
completed/in_review review queue is already deep enough to fill the
selection list, so the producer-review bottleneck is not overloaded.
Auditing, intake, and planning can still be dispatched — only the
implement tier is gated.

## Background

- Dispatch tier order (dispatchDowntimeWork): scheduled prompts → audit →
  implement → plan → intake. The code-freeze gate (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)
  already skips audit+implement during a release; this is a second,
  orthogonal implement-tier-only throttle on the producer-review queue.
- The herdr selection list displays up to `browseItemCount` items
  (default 20, clamp 1–50, packages/herdr/src/settings.ts).
- Review-queue count = completed/in_review **root** items
  (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`) —
  same query family as the audit tier (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG) and the
  selection list's mandatory review subset (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
  Operator decision (2026-08): count is ROOT-ONLY, not all items.
- Implement candidates carry `priority` (critical/high/medium/low) via
  parseImplementCandidatesOutput.

## Design notes

- Gate: when `reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount`, the implement tier
  selects only candidates with `priority === 'critical'`; non-critical
  candidates are excluded and dispatch falls through to plan/intake.
- Critical priority BYPASSES the gate — a critical implement always stays
  eligible regardless of queue depth.
- Fail-closed: a wl error counting the review queue → gate active (only
  critical implements), consistent with the code-freeze "ambiguous ⇒
  frozen" convention.
- `browseItemCount` is re-read live from settings on each dispatch (no
  plugin restart needed), matching the existing config() re-read pattern.
- The gate skip must NOT look like an empty backlog: when implement
  candidates exist but are gated AND plan/intake are empty, the outcome
  must be a neutral reason (never 'no-candidate'), so the worker's
  no-candidate cooldown is not triggered — polling continues and a
  critical implement / new plan / intake item dispatches immediately
  (mirrors the code-freeze 'code-freeze' reason convention).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A critical-priority implement candidate is always eligible regardless
   of review-queue depth (critical bypasses the gate).
2. When reviewQueueCount < browseItemCount, implement-tier selection is
   UNCHANGED: all priorities eligible; risk/effort/dispatched-marker
   filters unchanged.
3. When reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount, non-critical implement
   candidates are excluded; if only non-critical candidates remain,
   getNextImplementCandidate resolves null and dispatch falls through to
   plan/intake (no-candidate only when plan AND intake are genuinely
   empty; a gate skip with an empty plan/intake backlog is a neutral
   reason, never 'no-candidate').
4. The gate applies ONLY to the implement tier — audit, plan, intake,
   and scheduled-prompt dispatch are unaffected.
5. The review-queue count query is bounded by DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS and
   fail-closed (error ⇒ gate active).
6. Tests cover: gate boundary (count == listSize − 1 vs count == listSize),
   critical bypass, root-only counting, fall-through outcome, and the
   neutral (no-cooldown) reason on a gate skip with empty plan/intake.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — Audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit)
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — Code-freeze gate
- WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B — Selection list must always show all
  completed/in_review and critical items

As an operator, I do not want a transient failure in the downtime dispatch pipeline to strand a work item in `in_progress` with no agent working it and no automatic recovery.

## Background

- dispatchClaimedTier (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) pipeline: CAS claim → marker write → spawn.
- Gap 1 from the dispatch decision-point evaluation: if the marker write fails (D16) AFTER the CAS claim succeeds, the outcome is reason 'marker-write-failed' and the item stays `in_progress` — but the claim is never rolled back. The item is then invisible to every later tier: plan/implement tiers select `status === 'open'`, the audit tier selects `completed`. Only manual intervention recovers it.
- Same class of issue on 'spawn-failed' (D17): the marker stands (kind `implement`/`plan`/`audit` at the dispatched-at stage), so even after a human reverts the item to `open`, the dispatched-marker exclusion keeps it out of selection until the stage changes — a transient send-to-pi.sh failure (e.g. ENOENT) permanently removes a never-worked item from the idle-slot queue.
- Existing design intent (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 2): "an unmarked item is never dispatched" — this is sound; the gap is the missing RECOVERY path, not the fail-closed abort.

## Design notes

- Option A (rollback): on 'marker-write-failed', restore the item to its pre-claim state (CAS reverse: `wl update <id> --status open --if-status in_progress [--if-stage ...]`) so the next idle period can select it again.
- Option B (requeue for spawn-failed): on 'spawn-failed', write a distinct marker variant (e.g. `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries are already appended) and have the marker-exclusion readers treat a spawn-failed marker as NON-excluding (item is re-eligible) while still logging the failure — the rolling log already distinguishes attempted vs opened (WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U AC2).
- Both options preserve the fail-closed invariant (a marker-less item is never dispatched twice concurrently); the CAS claim already serializes re-selection.
- Decide and document whether the re-dispatch window should be immediate (next idle) or after a short backoff to avoid spawn-failure hot loops.

## Acceptance criteria

1. 'marker-write-failed' leaves the item in a state selectable by a future tier (rolled back to open+original stage, or equivalently recovered) — never stranded in_progress with no agent.
2. 'spawn-failed' does not permanently exclude the item from selection; the failure trace remains in the rolling log and the outcome is still not success.
3. No regression: an item with a STANDING success marker is still excluded (never double-dispatched); CAS claim still serializes concurrent panes.
4. Tests cover marker-write-failed and spawn-failed recovery paths end-to-end (claim → failure → re-selection on the next idle period).
data.title: Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (no permanent->in_progress stranding)

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.

# Dispatched audits: use both cheap slots during Phase 2 deep analysis

## Problem statement

The downtime worker pins `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` for dispatched audits (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) so an audit's Phase 2 child deep-analysis runs strictly sequentially (parent first, then one child at a time). This guarantees one audit fits cheap mode's 2-slots (parent + 1 child = 2) — but it also means a single dispatched audit NEVER uses more than one slot at a time during almost its entire run: Phase 1 is a single stream, and Phase 2 children serialize.

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22) shows the local model busy only ~25-38% while these audits ran — the second slot sat idle. The audit chain ran 17 child sessions with ~12s gaps, then multi-minute gaps between dispatched runs.

Raising the fan-out to 2 would let one child run concurrently with the parent (2 slots busy) during deep analysis — but the current bound (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) exists precisely to keep child-heavy audits inside the cheap 2-slot pool. Parent + 2 children = 3 concurrent streams would fall back to remote. This item must therefore be coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item so the combined in-flight stream budget never exceeds cheap capacity (2 slots).

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants higher overnight local utilization without pushing more traffic to fallback (429-capped) remotes.
- **Herdr downtime users** — want child-heavy audits to complete faster.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 2 deep-analysis concurrency for dispatched audits is mode-aware: 1 (current serial behavior) in fast mode or whenever the combined dispatch budget would exceed the cheap 2-slot pool; 2 when a second slot is genuinely free (coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item).
2. Parent + N children as a single audit run never produces more concurrent local streams than the cheap-mode slot budget (2 in cheap mode).
3. No audit-skill changes (agent-infrastructure boundary — the skill already honours the env var); change lives in `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
4. Tests: env var value is mode/budget-dependent; spawn options for cheap mode with a free second slot include `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '2'`; fast mode or full pool keeps `'1'`.
5. Measured outcome: dispatched audit Phase 2 wall-clock drops (children overlap the parent) and/or cheap-window busy % rises vs. the 25-38% baseline, without increasing remote fallback rate.

## Notes

- History: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (completed) set `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` with rationale "cheap mode = 2 slots = parent + 1 child" — the audit skill default is 2, which the bound overrode to prevent 3-stream fallback. This item revisits that bound for the slot-idle case rather than reverting it.
- Default `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` handling lives in `audit_runner.py` (`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM_ENV` / legacy alias) — pinned env in the pane spawn wins over the skill default.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (fan-out bound), plus the proxy usage report's recommendation #3.

# Faster downtime dispatch cadence: reduce poll interval and idle threshold

## Problem statement

The downtime worker polls the proxy status every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (default 10s, hard floor `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` = 10s) and requires the model to be continuously idle for `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 60s, floor 1s) before dispatching. Per dispatch cycle this imposes ~70s of scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn/claim overhead).

During the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22 proxy usage analysis) inter-run gaps of 141s, 146s and 312s were observed between consecutive dispatched runs — a large fraction (est. ~13% of the window) attributable to this threshold+poll+spawn cadence, on top of the model being idle ~50-68% of the time. The current 10s poll floor is a hard-coded guard ("must not hammer the proxy") rather than a measured load limit; the 60s idle threshold is a conservative default from the early worker design.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants more work dispatched into the idle overnight windows; lower latency between dispatch opportunities.
- **Herdr downtime users** — more items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both knobs stay configurable via downtime settings (existing `pollIntervalMs` / `idleThresholdMs` pattern) with **lowered floors**:
   - poll interval floor reduced from 10s to a measured-safe value (target 5s; assert proxy `/llama/local/status` call volume stays negligible — status endpoint is cheap and local);
   - idle threshold floor reduced to ≥1s (current floor) but adjusted production default lowered from 60s to a tuned value (target 15-30s) for the cheap window.
2. Defaults: cheap/downtime mode adopts the faster cadence; interactive or operator-session-sensitive paths unchanged.
3. The idle-gate semantics are preserved: dispatch still only occurs after the model has been continuously idle for the (shorter) threshold — no dispatch into a busy slot, no claim race with the existing single-flight safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
4. Tests updated: floor enforcement (values below floor rejected/clamped), cadence honored in the poll loop, idle-gate still requires the threshold to elapse, no dispatch while slots busy.
5. Measured outcome: mean inter-dispatch gap in the cheap window drops vs. baseline (146s/312s observed), and/or more sessions dispatched per night, without breaching proxy status-endpoint load limits.

## Notes

- Constants in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`: `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS = 10_000`, `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS = 1_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 60_000`.
- The 10s floor comment says "must not hammer the proxy" — quantify actual load before lowering; the status endpoint (`/llama/local/status`) is a cheap local JSON read, so the floor is expected to be safely reducible.
- Recommended: couple with the concurrent-dispatch item (bounded concurrency) so the faster cadence feeds more than one slot rather than just firing more single dispatches.
